newsitem.title: USA: Advisory firm says healthcare industry earnings up.
newsitem.headline: Advisory firm says healthcare industry earnings up.

text.p: The healthcare industry posted first quarter 1997 adjusted earnings growth of 11.4 percent on revenue gains of 15 percent, a private advisory firm said on Monday.
The analysis, released by WDI Capital Markets and KPMG Peat Marwick LLP's Health Ventures practice, examined the performance of more than 850 public companies, WDI and KPMG said in a statement.
The report focused on providers and services, biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, and medical devices and supply firms, they said.

Of those three sectors, the providers and services sectors reported the highest adjusted earnings growth, at 16.7 percent on revenue gains of 20 percent, a slight boost from a fourth quarter 1996 adjusted earnings increase of 16.1 percent, the report said.

WDI is an international advisory and investment banking firm that focuses on the the healthcare industry and KPMG Peat Marwick is a U.S. member firm of KPMG International, a professional services firm.
